title: Trillium Health - SOC2/ISO 27001 posture review
summary: High-level SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture review. Discussed trust center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO options, audit logging retention, KMS/encryption, and data residency. Agreed to share SOC2 report and controls-mapping template, schedule a technical deep dive and setup trial access to trust center. Some transcription artefacts and minor mis-attributions present.
topics: SOC 2 Type II report availability and scope
Controls mapping template for customer audit
Audit logs, retention, and export formats
Encryption at rest and KMS integrations
Data residency and regional hosting options
Next steps: share artifacts, schedule deep-dive
next_steps: Maya to send SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 statement of applicability link by 2026-05-14
Leon to schedule a technical deep-dive and demo of trust center for Priya and David (week of 2026-05-18)
Customer to fill and return initial controls mapping spreadsheet by 2026-05-21
Set up trial Trust Center access (read-only) for Eli and Priya
action_items: Maya Patel — Send SOC 2 Type II report (PDF) and pointer to Trust Center — due 2026-05-14
Leon Chen — Schedule technical deep-dive and provide link to Trust Center demo — due 2026-05-18
Priya Nair (Trillium) — Complete initial controls mapping spreadsheet and return — due 2026-05-21
Olivia Grant — Prepare short RBAC/SSO implementation note and SCIM examples — due 2026-05-15
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, our SE Leon and Olivia are here as well. We're here to go through your SOC 2 and ISO posture and any controls mapping questions.
[00:12] Sarah Lopez: Thanks, Maya. High level, we've got an internal audit coming up and we need to understand Redwood's attestation scope and whether you can support our mapping to ISO 27001.
[00:22] Leon Chen: Sure, happy to. Quick note - our SOC 2 Type II covers the security and availability trust services for the hosted platform, and we also have an ISO 27001 certificate for our control framework - I'll clarify scope in a moment.
[00:35] David Kim: Can you confirm data residency options? We need all PHI processing to remain in US regions for now.
[00:42] Olivia Grant: Yes, we have regional hosting options. For hosted customers we can pin to US-East or US-West regions; Private customers can run VPC/on-prem. There's also support for customer-managed keys if you need KMS/HSM.
[00:55] Priya Nair: On KMS - do you support Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) and integrate with AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault?
[01:02] Leon Chen: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and GCP Cloud KMS today; Azure is on our roadmap and we have a partnership effort underway. For BYOK, we can work through a KMS integration - some minor network configurations for Private deployments, but hosted can also use CMKs with restrictions.
[01:18] Sarah Lopez: Can you walk through audit logs? We need retention for 12 months and exportability to our SIEM.
[01:25] Maya Patel: Absolutely. We maintain detailed audit logs - admin actions, API calls, model deployments, config changes. Default retention on hosted plan is 90 days, but for enterprise we offer extended retention up to 24 months as an add-on. Logs can be streamed via syslog/S3 forwarding or pulled via API in JSON.
[01:40] Eli Fernandez: Are logs immutable? We need tamper-evidence for compliance.
[01:44] Leon Chen: Logs are write-once in our internal pipeline and we support signed delivery to customer S3 with object lock where available; we can discuss WORM/immutability for enterprise agreements.
[01:55] Sarah Lopez: Great. On controls mapping, do you have a template that maps SOC 2 controls to ISO 27001 clauses?
[02:02] Olivia Grant: Yes, we have a controls mapping spreadsheet we usually share. It shows our SOC 2 criteria, related ISO 27001 Annex A references, and evidence artifacts (policy docs, procedures, config screenshots). We'll share a redacted mapping you can use.
[02:16] David Kim: Also want to understand identity - SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and role-based access controls.
[02:22] Leon Chen: We support SAML SSO with SAML 2.0, OIDC on request, and SCIM provisioning for user sync. RBAC supports project-level roles, admin, auditor, viewer and custom roles. You can tie actions to least privilege and we have API tokens that are scoped.
[02:39] Priya Nair: Is there fine-grained permission to restrict model deployments or only org-level?
[02:44] Olivia Grant: You can set role-based restrictions at the project or model level depending on your plan; for Dedicated or Private deployments we can do even more granular controls.
[02:52] Sarah Lopez: For our audit we'll need evidence: the SOC 2 Type II PDF, ISO cert, a controls mapping, and evidence of SSO configuration and log exports. Can you provide those?
[03:01] Maya Patel: Yes - we'll provide the SOC 2 Type II report and ISO certificate, plus the controls mapping spreadsheet and example screenshots/transcripts for SSO and log exports. We'll mark which artifacts are acceptable for auditor review.
[03:12] David Kim: On encryption, can you confirm encryption at rest and in transit? Does Redwood manage keys or do we?
[03:19] Leon Chen: All data is TLS encrypted in transit. At rest we use AES-256. By default Redwood manages keys, but for enterprise customers we support customer-managed keys via KMS. Keys can be rotated per your policy.
[03:31] Priya Nair: Any PCI/HIPAA considerations? We're dealing with health data (PHI) and need to be careful about BAA.
[03:39] Maya Patel: We do not sign BAAs for every customer by default; Redwood has a BAA program and Private deployments are typically where we support HIPAA workloads. We'll loop in legal. For hosted customers, we have contractual modules and controls to support HIPAA requirements but we'll need to talk specifics.
[03:55] Eli Fernandez: Is Redwood's Trust Center public? Can we get read-only access to logs and reports?
[04:01] Olivia Grant: The Trust Center is a gated portal; we can provision read-only access to your security or compliance team after an NDA and account verification. It includes attestation docs, controls artifacts, and compliance FAQs.
[04:12] Sarah Lopez: Sounds good. About penetration testing and third-party assessments?
[04:17] Leon Chen: We run annual third-party penetration tests and external scans; results are summarized in the SOC 2 and there are remediation timelines. For high-risk findings we can share redacted executive summaries.
[04:28] Maya Patel: Quick note - sometimes transcription flips model names; if anything in the record looks off, we'll annotate.
[04:34] David Kim: On performance isolation - for Dedicated do you guarantee resource isolation and will that be in the SOC 2 scope?
[04:41] Leon Chen: Dedicated capacity provides hardware isolation and network isolation. The SOC 2 covers the control environment for our hosted platform; for Dedicated we include control overlays in our customer-facing docs and contractual SLAs.
[04:53] Priya Nair: For controls mapping do you align to ISO 27001:2013 Annex A?
[04:58] Olivia Grant: Yes, our mapping references Annex A controls and links them to SOC 2 criteria and internal policies; the spreadsheet has a column for ISO clause references.
[05:07] Sarah Lopez: For evidence, what format do you put settings in - screenshots, exports, or system logs?
[05:12] Maya Patel: We provide a mix: screenshots for config, syslog or S3 exports for logs, policy PDFs for governance, and signed attestations where needed. We'll flag which items are production-only and which are redacted.
[05:25] Eli Fernandez: Are there SLAs around data deletion and retention requests? We need to be able to demonstrate deletion for certain data categories.
[05:32] Leon Chen: We support data deletion APIs; for hosted we document retention periods and have procedures to delete customer data on request. For Private deployments you can run your own retention tooling. We'll provide the deletion workflow doc.
[05:45] Sarah Lopez: One risk area - if we use streaming inference, does Redwood retain prompts/inputs by default? We need clarity for PHI handling.
[05:53] Olivia Grant: By default, we retain minimal request metadata and logs for troubleshooting; customers can opt into longer retention for observability. For PHI use cases we recommend Private or Dedicated deployments with data-in-place and customer-managed keys, and we can sign tighter contractual terms.
[06:09] David Kim: How do you handle role auditing - list of who performed what and when?
[06:14] Leon Chen: That's part of the audit logs - admin actions, API keys usage, role changes. We include user identifiers, timestamps and the action type. These can be exported to your SIEM.
[06:25] Priya Nair: Ok, next steps?
[06:27] Maya Patel: We'll circulate materials: SOC 2 Type II PDF, ISO cert, controls mapping spreadsheet, Trust Center access steps. Leon will schedule a technical deep-dive with Priya and David. Please fill out the mapping sheet with any specific control gaps.
[06:40] Sarah Lopez: Good. Also can you provide a short note on encryption key rotation practices?
[06:45] Leon Chen: Yes, we'll include a one-page KMS/key rotation note in the artifacts.
[06:50] Eli Fernandez: We might ask for an architecture diagram showing where PHI touches the stack.
[06:54] Olivia Grant: We'll prepare a redacted architecture diagram showing data flows for hosted vs dedicated.
[07:00] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links and the next meeting invite.
[07:05] Sarah Lopez: Thanks all.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional filler words and imperfect proper nouns (e.g., "K-V cache" might be transcribed as "KV cash"). The call lasted ~45 minutes.

Action log (in transcript):
[07:20] Maya: I'll upload the SOC 2 and ISO artifacts to Trust Center and share links.
[07:26] Leon: I'll set up demo and deep-dive for next week.
[07:30] Olivia: I'll compile RBAC and SSO config snippets.

End of transcript.
